quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: ____ greatly increase stopping distances and crash severity.

options.text: High speeds
Slow speeds
Night drives
Uphill inclines

questions.correctAnswerText: High speeds
questions.explanation: High speeds greatly increase stopping distances and crash severity. The faster you drive, the harder your vehicle hits in a crash.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Continue normally through the intersection.
Stop and proceed when a green light appears.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means "caution." Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: You come to a flashing red light. You should:

options.text: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe to do so.
Stop only if other cars are also approaching the intersection.
Stop only if other cars are already within the intersection.
Slow down and be prepared to stop, if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop, check for other traffic, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?

options.text: Whoever started moving last
The driver
Whoever is slower
The pedestrian

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection, whether or not there is a traffic light or crosswalk.

questions.question: As a driver, you must stop at an intersection for a pedestrian:

options.text: Only if the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.
If the pedestrian is in a marked or unmarked crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is directly in front of your car.
Only if there is a separate "Walk" signal for pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the pedestrian is in a marked or unmarked crosswalk.
questions.explanation: You must stop for pedestrians crossing at any marked or unmarked crosswalk. Yield the right-of-way and proceed when the crosswalk is clear.

questions.question: Which of the following is true?

options.text: Drivers under 18 cannot text or talk on a cell phone while driving.
Drivers 18 and older must use a hands-free device when talking on a cell phone while driving.
Drivers 18 and older cannot text while driving.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In Oregon, drivers under 18 cannot talk or text on a cell phone while driving. Drivers 18 and older must use a hands-free device when using a cell phone.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Turn right after making a complete stop.
Right turns are not permitted.
Left turns are permitted.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right turns are not permitted.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign that shows a law you must obey. Right turns are not allowed where this sign is posted.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Wave your arms.
Use your emergency lights.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound your horn.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who might not see you. If you think another driver is about to hit you, sound your horn.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone
Only when driving in rural areas.
When driving under adverse weather conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you disrupt traffic flow. You can receive a ticket for driving too slowly.

questions.question: You may not park:

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must be within 12 inches of the curb.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle:

options.text: At a stop sign.
At a red light.
When a traffic officer tells you to stop.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, red lights, and when a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: It is best to keep space around your vehicle:

options.text: Only behind your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space on all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left or right.

questions.question: When another vehicle is tailgating you:

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If no right lane exists, wait for clear road ahead and slowly reduce speed to let the tailgater pass.
Never brake suddenly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If tailgated and a right lane is open, move to it. If no right lane exists, wait until the road ahead is clear, then slowly reduce speed to encourage the tailgater to pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of being hit from behind.

questions.question: A steady yellow light means:

options.text: Go.
Yield to other cars.
Slow down and prepare to stop.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and prepare to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light warns that a red light is coming soon. Slow down and be ready to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, drive through carefully.

questions.question: What does an orange sign indicate?

options.text: Start of a no passing zone.
Railroad crossing ahead.
School zone ahead.
Construction work ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols warn of construction, maintenance, or emergency work.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Keep driving in your lane.
Pull to the right side and stop.
Stop where you are immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear a siren, pull to the right side of the road and stop immediately.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Stop.
Side road.
Two-way left turn.
Farm machinery.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs mean stop. Come to a complete stop and yield the right-of-way. You may proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: A bicyclist who breaks traffic laws:

options.text: Does not have to follow traffic laws.
Can be ticketed.
Will always get a warning.
Will have their bicycle taken away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be ticketed.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights, duties, and responsibilities as drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Avoid sudden stops.
Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas pedal to slow down before using the brakes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to avoid hitting you. Release the gas pedal first to slow your vehicle, then apply steady brake pressure to stop smoothly and activate your brake lights.

questions.question: Before passing another vehicle, signal:

options.text: Just before changing lanes.
At any time.
After changing lanes.
Early so others know your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early so others know your plans.
questions.explanation: Signal early before passing so other drivers know what you plan to do.

questions.question: You are driving at night and a car is coming toward you. Dim your headlights when the other car is within:

options.text: 500 feet.
400 feet.
450 feet.
350 feet.

questions.correctAnswerText: 500 feet.
questions.explanation: Switch to low beam headlights when an oncoming vehicle is within 500 feet of your car.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.
Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
Allow the motorcycle to use only half of a lane.
Pass using the same lane as the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle needs a full lane width, just like any other vehicle. Even if there seems to be room to share a lane, motorcycles need space to move safely.

questions.question: You should honk your horn when you:

options.text: Are traveling through an intersection.
Are passing a bicyclist.
See a child who is about to run into the street.
Are parallel parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: See a child who is about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn others when they may not see you. For example, honk if a child starts to run into the street in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: Defensive driving is:

options.text: Identifying dangerous driving situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
Defending yourself against poor drivers by getting ahead of them in traffic.
Following the vehicle ahead of you at a close distance.
Quickly changing lanes and shifting in and out of traffic congestion.

questions.correctAnswerText: Identifying dangerous driving situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means spotting dangerous situations and acting before an accident happens. It helps you avoid crashes caused by aggressive, careless, or impaired drivers.

questions.question: When you see other drivers acting or reacting in anger:

options.text: Don't make eye contact.
Don't react with hand gestures.
Distance yourself from the situation.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Avoid eye contact and hand gestures. Slow down, move over, or do whatever is safe to stay away from an angry driver.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.
Busy sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a pedestrian crossing area. Watch for people crossing and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Taking drugs along with alcohol:

options.text: Increases the risk of causing a crash.
Is no more dangerous than consuming alcohol by itself.
Lessens the effect of alcohol on your ability to drive.
Has no effect on your general driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of causing a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal) harm your ability to drive safely. Mixing alcohol with drugs makes crashes much more likely.

questions.question: This road sign indicates:

options.text: The maximum safe speed for a residential area.
The maximum safe speed for an expressway exit.
The maximum safe speed for an expressway entrance.
The maximum safe speed for a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed for an expressway exit.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the safe speed limit for exiting a highway. For example, it may show 30 mph.

questions.question: Work zone signs mean:

options.text: It is summer.
You must immediately stop and back up.
Less than ideal conditions are present for driving.
You should drive faster to get out of the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less than ideal conditions are present for driving.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and mean work is being done on or near the road. Drive with extra care.

questions.question: If you are driving on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches, you must:

options.text: Drive with your flashers turned on.
Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches on a one-way street, move to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: Railroad crossing signals are flashing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the vehicle ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: You must stop at least 15 feet from the railroad tracks when warning signals flash. Watch for other signs of an oncoming train, such as lowered gates or train sounds.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass, even if it could be dangerous.
Lanes move in opposite directions.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction. A dashed white line means you can cross it to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: Which statement about passing is true?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before passing. Make sure no cars are coming toward you.
Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot before passing left.
Wait until you see both headlights of the car you passed in your rearview mirror before moving back to your lane.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When passing, always signal 100 feet ahead. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for blind spots. Wait until you see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line between lanes mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
Both lanes travel in the same direction.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass, even if it could be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. A dashed yellow line means both directions can pass if it is safe. Only pass if no oncoming traffic will be affected.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Running the car in the driveway.
Accelerating quickly.
Slowing down gradually.
Braking abruptly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down gradually.
questions.explanation: Quick stops waste fuel because your car uses gas to speed back up. Looking ahead lets you slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid sudden braking. This improves gas mileage.
